newsitem.title: USA: Panel decides to exclude Perot from debates.
newsitem.headline: Panel decides to exclude Perot from debates.

text.p: A bipartisan commission planning for the U.S. presidential debates has voted to recommend that third-party candiate Ross Perot be excluded from the debates between President Bill Clinton and Republican Bob Dole, a source close to Dole said on Tuesday.
"We have been informed that Perot has been excluded from all debates," the source in the Dole campaign told Reuters.

The Dole campaign quickly hailed the decision, issuing a statement saying: "The unanimous decision today by the Commission on Presidential Debates to move forward on debates without the presence of third party candidates was the right one."

The commission, led by former chairmen of the Republican and Democratic parties, was to formally announce its recommendations on conduct of three proposed 1996 presidential debates at noon in Washington (1600 GMT). It was formed in an attempt to take organization of the debates -- which have become crucial elements in U.S. presidential elections -- out of the partisan arena. Its decisions are not binding, however, and also need to be agreed to by the Clinton campaign.

The Clinton campaign had said it would welcome Perot into the debates but Dole's team had opposed his inclusion, fearing he might siphon more votes away from their struggling candidate than from the front-running Democratic president.

The decision to exclude the outspoken Texas billionaire will surely stir widespread controversy. He won 19 percent of the popular vote in 1992 after starring in that year's debates as a folksy, cranky advocate of federal budget-balancing and campaign reform. This year, however, he has attracted only single-digit opinion poll backing as leader of the new Reform Party.
